user_intent.goal: Unify webview UI and settings.json configuration experience for consistent plugin usage
user_intent.scope: Configuration services, settings managers, webview UI sync
key_constraints: Bidirectional sync between webview UI and settings.json
No default value pollution in settings.json
Both user groups must have identical experience
Backward compatibility with existing settings.json values

critical.rationale: Core bidirectional sync service - primary implementation target for F-002, F-003
Feature settings storage - needs dirtyKeys support for F-001
Webview message handler - needs dirtyKeys message contract extension for F-001

high.rationale: Config change listener - triggers sync from settings.json side
Extension activation - SettingsSyncService initialization and initialSync
Frontend component - needs dirty state tracking (F-001), save button, sync toggle banner (F-002)

medium.rationale: Message type definitions - needs new UIRequest types for sync toggle
Config schema - needs description improvements for F-005

prioritized_context.sorting_rationale: Based on data flow: types first, then sync service (core), then managers/handlers (middleware), then frontend, then activation

conflict_detection.rationale: Brainstorm session already resolved all architectural decisions. Settings-sync-service.ts already implements bidirectional sync. Changes are additive (dirty tracking, toggle, classification) rather than structural.

potential_conflicts.description: New file, no existing consumers to conflict with

constraints: MUST NOT break backward compatibility with existing settings.json values
MUST support both global and workspace scope
Sync toggle stored in globalState, not settings.json
globalState remains runtime source of truth
API keys remain in Secret Storage (not settings.json directly)
dirtyKeys field is optional for backward compatibility
